name: ECSMarketplaceDataUpload — Marketplace Data Ingestion Service
summary: Containerized Python service that ingests seller reports (orders, inventory, returns, ads, promos, fees, payouts) from many marketplaces into PostgreSQL and triggers downstream profitability jobs.
source_path: Not in this workspace (company code). Documented from Learning My Forcesight code/LEARNING_GUIDE.md and resume.
evidence_note: Self-reported: resume + generated study guide. Numbers differ between sources (20+ vs 30+ channels; 150+ processors vs 170+ report types) — align them before interviews.
purpose_md: Each marketplace (Swiggy, Blinkit, Zepto, Myntra, Nykaa, Snapdeal, Amazon Vendor Central, Flipkart, BigBasket, FirstCry…) sends reports in different formats (CSV, XLSX, XLS, XLSB, ZIP, PDF). Brands need **unified order, inventory and fee data** for profitability dashboards. This service normalises every report type into common `orders` and `inventory` tables.
architecture_md:
```
User uploads file → S3 → API Gateway → lambda_handler
  → MODULE_DISPATCH[moduleName] (lazy import)
  → read_and_validate() → pandas transform
  → PostgreSQL upsert → fs_upload status update
  → async invoke profitability Lambda
```
- **Registry/dispatcher**: one entry point, `_MODULE_SPECS` tuple maps `MODULE_NAME → (python file, function, body keys)`. Modules are imported lazily to keep cold start small.
- **Shared `DatabaseManager`** (helper.py, ~3,700 lines): DB connection, file I/O, upserts, org config, invoice-type detection, Lambda invoke.
- **Two trigger modes**: manual upload (single file via API) and automation (`requestId` → DynamoDB `fs-sync-requests-db` → batch of S3 files).
- Packaged as a container and run on ECS (resume); guide describes the Lambda-style handler.
folder_structure_md:
```
ECSMarketplaceDataUpload/
├── lambda_function.py      # entry point + module registry
├── lambda_test.py          # local harness simulating API Gateway events
├── helper.py               # DatabaseManager, S3, file I/O, upserts
├── bootstrap_config.py     # dotenv + pandas config
├── Dockerfile
├── SwiggyOrders.py, BlinkitOrders.py, Zepto_Orders.py …   # per-channel processors
├── MyntraSORSummaryReport.py
├── BlinkitMPFees.py        # shared promo/fee calculator
├── status_map.py           # order status → fsorderstatus
├── snapdeal_helpers.py, snapdeal_autosync.py, swiggyAutomationProcessor.py
└── postalCodes.json        # district → pincode/state lookup
```
modules_md:
- `lambda_function.py` — entry point, registry, routing
- `helper.py` — `DatabaseManager`: `read_and_validate`, `insert_fs_upload`, `update_fs_upload_status`, `upsert_data_do_nothing`, `upsert_data_with_deadlock_handling`, `fetchDashboard`, `detect_invoice_price_type`, `invoke_lambda_function`
- `SwiggyOrders.py` — template quick-commerce processor
- `MyntraSORSummaryReport.py` — complex multi-report SOR logic with `credIndex` multi-dashboard support
- `BlinkitMPFees.py` — promo/fee calculator reused by Swiggy, Blinkit, Zepto
- `snapdeal_autosync.py` — multi-file batch automation + ECS profit task
database_md:
| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `inventory` | SKU master — MRP, price, COGS, brand |
| `orders` | Order line items — invoiceprice, settledamount, marketplacefees |
| `fs_upload` | Upload job tracking — UUID, status (Processing/Completed/Error), message |
| `fs-organisations-channels-db` | Per-org config — brands, commission %, invoice type |
| `bankstatement` | Payment settlement data |

Upserts: inventory `ON CONFLICT (id, orgid) DO NOTHING`; orders `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET col = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.col, table.col)`.
apis_md:
- **Inbound**: API Gateway event — `requestContext.authorizer.org_id`, JSON body with `moduleName`, `URL`, `channel`.
- **AWS**: S3 presigned URL download (`requests`), `boto3` Lambda async invoke (`profitability-fmcg`, `ProfitabilityAllChannelsPostgres`), ECS `run_task` (`estimate-and-profit-postgres-V2-service`), DynamoDB `fs-sync-requests-db`. Region ap-south-1.
business_logic_md:
**Invoice types** (per-org config) decide how revenue, fees and settlement are calculated:
- `MRP%` — revenue = MRP × qty × commission %
- `ASP` — revenue = actual selling price from report
- `GMV` — gross merchandise value
- Myntra SOR: `NET_SALES_FINAL_PAYABLE` (invoice = price × qty, settled = COGS × qty, fees = invoice − settled) vs `FINAL_PAYABLE_BOTH` (fees 0)

**Standard processor pipeline**: insert_fs_upload → read_and_validate → fetchDashboard → brand filtering → processInventory → upsert DO NOTHING → processOrders (+fees) → upsert with deadlock retry → mark Completed → invoke profitability.
challenges_md:
- Every marketplace uses different formats, sheet names and column headers, and changes them without notice.
- Concurrent order writes on distributed Postgres (Citus) caused **deadlocks**.
- Re-uploads must update orders without wiping existing non-null values.
- Lambda cold starts with 150+ modules.
- Users need to see upload progress and clear errors.
solutions_md:
- `read_and_validate()` detects file type, resolves sheets, matches columns case-insensitively, and returns a clear error listing missing columns.
- Retry loop on `DeadlockDetected`.
- `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.col, table.col)` in `DO UPDATE` keeps existing values when the new file has nulls; inventory uses `DO NOTHING`.
- Lazy imports via the registry.
- `fs_upload` status table (Processing → Completed/Error + message).
contributions_md: From resume: primary developer (**1,000+ commits, ~68% of all commits**); personally wrote **150+ report processors**; designed the config-driven dispatcher with lazy loading and the upload status tracker; built automated report sync for 6 channels (DynamoDB jobs, S3 files, per-file success/failure analytics); connection pooling, transactional writes, bulk upserts; robust parsing of CSV/XLSX/XLSB/ZIP/PDF.
learnings_md:
_Write this in your own words._ Prompts:
- Why is a registry better than a long if/elif chain here?
- When would you choose DO NOTHING vs DO UPDATE?
- What would you change if you rebuilt it today (tests? queue? schema validation per report?)
pending_improvements_md: _Ideas, not facts:_ automated tests per processor with fixture files; per-report schema definitions; structured logging with upload UUID; a dead-letter path for failed files.

items.title: Automated report sync for 6 channels (DynamoDB + S3)
Deadlocks under concurrent order upserts (Citus) — retry loop

name: Insta Post Downloader
summary: Local FastAPI web app that downloads Instagram posts or whole profiles with live progress.
evidence_note: Source code read: app.py (134 lines), downloader.py (463 lines), static/index.html (358 lines).
purpose_md: Download an Instagram profile's posts (or a single post by URL) to a local folder, optionally logged in, with progress shown in the browser.
architecture_md:
- `app.py` — FastAPI routes; jobs kept in an in-memory `dict[str, JobState]`.
- `POST /api/download` creates a job id and starts `run_download` in a thread via `loop.run_in_executor`.
- `GET /api/jobs/{id}/events` streams job snapshots as **Server-Sent Events** (`StreamingResponse`, `text/event-stream`), polling every 0.4s and sending only changes.
- `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel` sets a `threading.Event` the worker checks.
- `downloader.py` wraps instaloader: session reuse, login with 2FA/bad-credential handling, a fail-fast `RateController`, and a path-traversal guard (`_safe_under`).
folder_structure_md:
```
InstaPostDownloader/
├── app.py            # FastAPI routes + job registry
├── downloader.py     # instaloader wrapper, JobState dataclass
├── static/index.html # UI
├── downloads/        # output (served at /media)
├── sessions/         # saved login sessions
├── requirements.txt
└── run.bat
```
modules_md:
- `parse_target` / `normalize_username` — accept username or post URL
- `JobState` dataclass with `cancel: threading.Event`
- `FailFastRateController` — stop instead of sleeping on 429
- `fetch_profile`, `fetch_post`, `run_download`, `list_downloaded_accounts`
database_md: None — in-memory job dict; files on disk.
business_logic_md: Maps instaloader exceptions (ProfileNotExists, LoginRequired, TooManyRequests, TwoFactorAuthRequired, BadCredentials, Connection) to friendly `DownloadError` messages returned as HTTP 400.
challenges_md: Instagram rate-limits and login requirements; long-running downloads that must not block the event loop; cancellation mid-download.
solutions_md: Blocking work in executor threads; `asyncio.to_thread` for profile lookups; SSE for progress; `threading.Event` for cooperative cancellation; fail-fast rate controller.
contributions_md: Personal project. _Note how much was written by hand vs. with AI help._
learnings_md: _Write this in your own words._ Prompts: Why SSE instead of WebSockets? What happens to jobs if the server restarts? Why must blocking calls leave the event loop?
pending_improvements_md: _Ideas:_ persist jobs; tests for `parse_target`; limit concurrent jobs.

interview.q: In your downloader apps, why did you run downloads with run_in_executor instead of directly inside the async route?
Explain how your Server-Sent Events progress stream works and its limitations.

name: YouTube Playlist Downloader (Web)
summary: Local FastAPI web app around yt-dlp for downloading playlists or single songs as audio/video with live progress.
evidence_note: Source code read: app.py (139 lines), downloader.py (569 lines), static/index.html (429 lines). Same job/SSE architecture as Insta Post Downloader.
purpose_md: Look up a YouTube playlist/video URL, then download audio or video at a chosen quality into organised folders.
architecture_md: Same pattern as Insta Post Downloader: in-memory jobs, executor thread workers, SSE progress, `threading.Event` cancel. `downloader.py` parses URLs (`urlparse`/`parse_qs`, regex-validated IDs), builds yt-dlp options per media/quality, locates ffmpeg, and maps yt-dlp errors to friendly messages.

```
YoutubePlaylistDownloader/
├── app.py
├── downloader.py
├── static/index.html
├── downloads/
├── requirements.txt

```
modules_md:
- `parse_url` — validates hosts and IDs (VIDEO_ID_RE, PLAYLIST_ID_RE)
- `fetch_target` — metadata lookup
- `_download_format_opts`, `_output_template` — yt-dlp configuration
- `run_download` — progress hooks feeding `JobState`
- `_friendly_ytdlp_error`, `_safe_under`
challenges_md: yt-dlp needs ffmpeg and a JS runtime; progress reporting from a library callback in another thread.
solutions_md: ffmpeg location via imageio-ffmpeg fallback; progress hooks update a shared JobState snapshot read by the SSE stream.

name: iPhone → Android Media Converter
summary: CLI that converts HEIC photos to JPEG and MOV/HEVC videos to H.264 MP4 for Android.
source_path: F:\Personal Projects\Iphone to Android Media convert
purpose_md: Make iPhone media playable on Android without visible quality loss.
architecture_md: argparse CLI (`--input`, `--output`, `--recursive`, `--photo-quality`, `--crf`, `--preset`, `--audio-bitrate`) → collect files → per file: Pillow (RGB convert, JPEG q95, subsampling=0) or ffmpeg subprocess (libx264, CRF 18, yuv420p, +faststart, AAC) → per-file try/except so one failure doesn't stop the batch.
challenges_md: HEIC isn't supported by Pillow by default; colour modes (RGBA/P) can't be saved as JPEG.

name: Scratch to Pro — English Communication Trainer
summary: Next.js app for English practice: levelled lessons, grammar drills, spaced-repetition review and AI coaching/role-play via an OpenAI-compatible API.
source_path: F:\Personal Projects\English Learning Sctrach to Pro
evidence_note: Source code read: lib/ai.ts, lib/review.ts, api/coach/route.ts, lib/backup.ts (~5,800 lines TS/TSX + JSON content). Built with Claude Code (.claude folder). Git repo with 1 commit (2026-11-12).
purpose_md: Take an English learner from basics to professional interviews with lessons, drills and AI feedback.
architecture_md: App Router pages (levels/[level]/[module]/[lesson], grammar/[topic], review, practice, ai-chat, dashboard). Route handlers `/api/coach`, `/api/ai-chat`, `/api/grammar-ai` validate input with zod, call the LLM in JSON mode and validate the output with zod. `getAi()` tries a comma-separated list of models, falling back on 404/429/500/503/timeouts (25s timeout, no SDK retries).

```
src/
├── app/ (pages + api route handlers)
├── components/ (LessonPlayer, ReviewSession, AiChat, …)
├── content/*.json (lessons, grammar, exercises)
└── lib/ (ai, review, progress, mastery, backup, speech)
```

- `lib/ai.ts` — provider-agnostic client with model fallback
- `lib/review.ts` — Leitner deck (intervals 0,1,3,7,16,35) for vocab, quiz, corrections, exercises
- `lib/backup.ts` — JSON export/import of all localStorage keys
database_md: localStorage (`scratch-to-pro-*` keys). A leftover `prisma/dev.db` exists but Prisma isn't a dependency.
apis_md: OpenAI-compatible chat completions (Gemini by default per .env.example).
